question.problem:
Find $\text{E}[\frac{Y}{7X}],$ given that random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{21}{4}{x}^{2}y,\, & -1\le x\le 1,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are continuous random variables, and $f(x,y)$ is their joint probability density function. If $r:{R}^{2}\to R$ is a function of two variables, then the rule of the lazy statistician states that

$$
\text{E}[r(X,Y)]={∬}_{{R}^{2}}r(x,y)\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
r(x,y)=\frac{y}{7x}.
$$

Now, let's sketch the region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 1,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le 1\},$ where $f(x,y)$ is nonzero.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14154787/assets/54777bc840acd1d1c24da08ccb99025b039af9c47421602a3d9dd73df2a91779.png)

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[\frac{Y}{7X}] & ={∬}_{{R}^{2}}\frac{y}{7x}\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{y}{7x}\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{1}\frac{y}{7x}\cdot \frac{21}{4}{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{4}{\int }_{-1}^{1}x{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{1}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{4}{\int }_{-1}^{1}x{[\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{y={x}^{2}}^{y=1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{4}{\int }_{-1}^{1}x[\frac{1}{3}-\frac{{x}^{6}}{3}]\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{-1}^{1}(x-{x}^{7})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-\frac{{x}^{8}}{8}]}_{x=-1}^{x=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{8})-(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{8})] \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
